sec: Subacute Thyroiditis Triphasic Curve & Postpartum Comparison

items.q: What initial mechanism triggers the clinical presentation and thyrotoxic phase of subacute thyroiditis?
opts: Stored hormone release from damaged thyroid follicles
New autonomous hormone hyper-synthesis driven by TRAb
Excessive peripheral T4 to T3 conversion by deiodinase-2
Ectopic thyroid tissue activation in ovarian teratoma
items.exp: Under mechanism: 'Stored hormone release -> ↑ Free T3, ↑ Free T4, ↓ TSH, T3/T4 < 15'. (Book p915)

items.q: Match the early presentation findings of subacute thyroiditis — 1) Systemic sign 2) Gland pain 3) Inflammatory marker … A) Fever > 2 weeks B) Neck pain / sore throat / ear pain C) Markedly elevated ESR (↑↑ ESR)
items.exp: Early presentation: Fever > 2 weeks; Pain in the gland: Neck pain / Sore throat / Ear pain; and ↑↑ ESR. (Book p915)

items.q: Once stored hormones are exhausted in subacute thyroiditis, what percentage of patients develop permanent hypothyroidism?
items.exp: Under mechanism: 'Stored hormone exhausted -> Hypothyroid (In 15% Permanent hypothyroid) -> Recovery'. (Book p915)

items.q: A 38-year-old woman presents with severe neck pain radiating to her ears, fever for 2 weeks, high ESR, and suppressed TSH with high free T4 (T3/T4 ratio < 15). What is the drug of choice (DOC) and its dose?
items.exp: Under management: 'Aspirin 600 mg Q6H (DOC)', NSAIDS, Steroids. (Book p915)

items.q: On the clinical course graph of subacute thyroiditis, match the time interval to its corresponding phase — 1) 0 - 6 weeks 2) 6 - 12 weeks 3) 12 - 18 weeks … A) Thyrotoxic phase (high urinary/serum T4, high ESR, low TSH) B) Hypothyroid phase (TSH rising, T4 falling) C) Recovery phase (normalization)
items.exp: The graph shows: 0-6 weeks is the toxic phase; 6-12 weeks is the hypothyroid phase; 12-18 weeks is the recovery phase. (Book p915)

items.q: Which of the following conditions is NOT associated with an elevated TSH level in the summary note on page 915?
opts: TSH Adenoma and recovery phase of thyroiditis
items.exp: Central hypothyroidism has a 'Normal TSH level' (with low peripheral hormones); elevated TSH is seen in 1° hypothyroid, RTH, TSH adenoma, and recovery phase of thyroiditis. (Book p915)

items.q: Per the summary note on page 915, what does a normal TSH level signify in a patient with low circulating thyroid hormones?
opts: Early toxic phase of subacute thyroiditis
items.exp: Page 915 explicitly states: 'Normal TSH level : Central hypothyroidism'. (Book p915)

items.q: Postpartum thyroiditis is also known as ___ or ___ thyroiditis.
items.exp: Under Postpartum thyroiditis: 'AKA Painless / silent thyroiditis'. (Book p915)

items.q: Match the autoimmune diseases associated with postpartum thyroiditis — 1) Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) 2) Sjogren's syndrome 3) Endocrine / skin autoimmune … A) Connective tissue disease B) Exocrine gland sicca syndrome C) Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) / Vitiligo
items.exp: Postpartum thyroiditis is seen in association with autoimmune diseases: SLE, Sjogren's syndrome, T1DM, and Vitiligo. (Book p915)

items.q: Compare pain and pregnancy timing in Subacute vs Postpartum thyroiditis: I Neck pain is present in subacute thyroiditis, but absent/silent in postpartum thyroiditis. II Subacute thyroiditis has no association with pregnancy, whereas postpartum thyroiditis occurs post partum.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Table comparisons: Pain is Present in subacute, Absent/silent in postpartum; Association with pregnancy is No in subacute, Post Partum in postpartum. (Book p915)

items.q: From the subacute vs postpartum thyroiditis comparison table, match the lab/treatment characteristics — 1) ESR 2) Anti-TPO antibody 3) Role of steroids … A) Subacute: ↑↑ ESR; -ve TPO Ab; Steroids: Yes B) Postpartum: Normal ESR; +ve TPO Ab; Steroids: No (β-blocker can be used)
items.exp: Subacute has ↑↑ ESR, -ve TPO Ab, and steroids are useful (Yes); Postpartum has normal ESR, +ve TPO Ab, and no steroids (β-blockers used). (Book p915)

items.q: Assess autoimmunity in these thyroiditides: I Subacute thyroiditis is an autoimmune disease. II Postpartum thyroiditis is an autoimmune disease with positive anti-TPO antibodies.
opts: I is false; II is true
Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Table shows: Autoimmune is 'No' for Subacute thyroiditis, and 'Yes' for Postpartum thyroiditis. (Book p915)
